{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABYZNM-w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6PzhB9I7Y", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 84, "title": "Experiment with latest upstream Bullet in a custom Ammo.js WASM build", "body": "## Problem

The Examples and physics regression tests now use the WASM variant of `ammojs-typed@1.1.0` (#82 / PR #83), but this **did not upgrade Bullet**: the upstream Ammo.js implementation documents **Bullet 2.82 + a 2.83 raycast patch**. The maintainer wants to try **the newest available official Bullet source**, especially because persistent severe MMD physics instability has sometimes been observed at **120 FPS** but is not yet reproducibly explained.

Verified upstream context on 2026-10-20:
- Official Bullet latest GitHub **release**: [3.25](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/releases/tag/3.25) (published 2022-04-24).
- The official [`bulletphysics/bullet3` `master`](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3) has **newer commits**; last checked SHA `d3afe76132fc76b0f9b2359cbaef47a3766e7fbb` (2026-10-09). An experimental build from a pinned current upstream master revision best matches the request for the *latest code*, not merely the newest tagged release. Recheck and record the exact chosen upstream SHA at implementation.
- [`ammojs3`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ammojs3) claims to have been built with Bullet 3.26, but is an older third-party package with unclear npm license metadata. It is **not** evidence that 3.26 is the latest *official release*, and must not be adopted for distribution without checking provenance, license, binary reproducibility and API compatibility.

## Expected outcome

Produce a **reproducible experimental Ammo.js WebAssembly build** from the newest suitable *official* Bullet source, exposing the subset of Ammo/Bullet APIs used by three-mmd-loader. Run a controlled **old-Bullet WASM vs newest-Bullet WASM** comparison without changing any MMD physics parameters or silently replacing the production/default backend.

Prefer a small, documented Emscripten/WebIDL-based build and compatibility adapter over rewriting Bullet's physics engine or prematurely switching the entire library to custom native bindings. If current upstream master cannot be built compatibly, document the specific blocker; optionally establish an official Bullet 3.25 tagged reference build as a separate comparison. **Do not label a fallback to 3.25 as “latest master.”**

### Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Re-verify the latest official Bullet release and newest upstream commit at implementation time; pin and document the **exact Bullet source commit/tag**, source origin, relevant patches, Emscripten version, build flags, output licenses, and reproducible build commands. No floating `master` dependency in test artifacts.
- [ ] Build a real **WebAssembly + JavaScript glue** Ammo-compatible runtime using that Bullet source, with binary loading in browsers and **classic Workers**. Keep original Bullet attribution/license and check all redistributed dependencies and binaries. A prebuilt third-party `ammojs3` may be evaluated only after provenance/licensing checks.
- [ ] Preserve or explicitly adapt the APIs required by `src/ammo.ts` and `MMDPhysics`, including rigid-body construction, `btGeneric6DofSpringConstraint`, shapes, worlds, motion states, additional damping, collision filters, `setParam` / STOP_ERP where supported, resource destruction and worker initialization. Fail with actionable diagnostics if an API or binary is incompatible; no silent fallback presented as the newest Bullet.
- [ ] Offer a **reversible, clearly labeled A/B selection** in a test/Example harness. Keep existing `ammojs-typed@1.1.0` WASM **the default**, and run both variants with the same scene, model metadata, physics code, gravity, fixed timestep `1/60`, `maxStepNum=10`, ERP, damping, collision settings, initial poses and timestamps. Do not simultaneously introduce 1/120 step, frame-offset or kinematic-control changes.
- [ ] Test PMD and PMX rigid bodies, spring joints, linked collisions, bone types (particularly type 2), animation/IK, standalone/shared **Sync**, and **Worker** (including successful init, communication and fallback). Include browser/WASM loading tests that check actual `WebAssembly.Instance` and wasm exports, not just filename.
- [ ] Compare **60 / 120 / 144 FPS** with repeatable elapsed-time tapes and at least one animated kinematic-anchor + joint/dynamic-body fixture. Record executed Bullet steps, wall-clock-equivalent simulated time, finite transforms, body/bone trajectories, divergences, initialization and per-step costs. Avoid claims about physics speed or stability based solely on synthetic averages.
- [ ] Run applicable typecheck, unit/integration/browser tests, local build and locally served Examples. Preserve existing tests and documented consumer-supplied Ammo behavior.
- [ ] Summarize whether latest Bullet produces better, unchanged, or worse reproducible behavior. **The intermittent violent-oscillation bug is not “fixed” unless actually reproduced and shown resolved**; do not require that outcome for this experimental task. Keep rollback straightforward.

### Required post-merge verification

- **PENDING until run:** If the experiment changes deployed Examples, inspect the **latest attempt** of the merge-triggered GitHub Pages deployment, record the deployed SHA, verify newly published glue/WASM bytes, MIME/paths and error-free loading. Publication is not a pre-merge condition.
- **PENDING until run:** If the A/B harness is published, smoke-test the actual public browser examples for both old and new Bullet WASM, including Sync and Worker. Record browser, URLs, backend evidence, timestamps and failures. Keep these checks separate from pre-merge automated tests.
- **Optional, non-blocking maintainer follow-up:** Compare long-running natural 120 Hz motion on real PMD/PMX hair/skirt models for visually apparent instability. Record observations without claiming a confirmed fix from CI or a short smoke test.

## Context

- Current [three-mmd-loader MMDPhysics](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts), [structural Ammo API](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/ammo.ts), [WASM Examples bootstrap](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/examples/ammo-runtime.ts), and [Worker setup](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysicsWorker.ts).
- [Official Bullet sources and releases](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3), [upstream Ammo.js (Bullet version documented)](https://github.com/kripken/ammo.js#upstream-version).
- [babylon-mmd](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/docs/docs/reference/runtime/bullet-physics/index.md) integrates a newer Bullet with custom Rust/C++ WASM bindings; that is a reference, **not** a request to copy its full runtime architecture into this experiment.
- Previous WASM-only switch: [Issue #82](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/82) / [PR #83](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/pull/83). The purpose of this Issue is specifically **upgrading the Bullet engine behind WASM**, not repeating that work.
